## Chapter Fourteen

Last Supper



The next morning Lucas got up early and made breakfast, by the time Job stumbled out of his bedroom Lucas had a plate for both of them along with coffee ready for him. “Oh, looks like your hired” the older man said jokingly digging into the eggs and toast. “If I have some time today, I need to find some items to put together a target and a training dummy for my room, if that’s okay?” he asked his friend, Job nodded “Go see Sally, he will be able to get you what you need”. Lucas nodded and they both finished breakfast making small talk as roommates do in the morning.

Lucas left the store an hour later, snow covered the ground an inch having fell the night before, even with the crumbling buildings it gave the row of townhouses he walked by a serene look. He carefully made his way towards the old marine barracks and down the snow-covered stairs to stand in front of the rusted iron door. Lucas knocked three times and waited, he repeated this and by the time he finished the second set of knocks, the peep hole opened, and chow’s eyes set upon him disinterested “Nice red slippers, where did ya get em” he asked. Lucas sighed “Definitely not in Kansas” he responded, wondering where the hell the reference was from. He opened the door and let Lucas down the hall to the dancefloor of the club. As he descended the stairs, he noticed Rollie sweeping the debris covered floor, the young black man waved at Lucas who enthusiastically returned it “Hey Rollie, what’s new?” he asked smiling at the other man. Rollie just shrugged “Same shit my friend” and returned the smile.

“Sally came out of the backroom resplendent in his pink Kimono and wig “Job called; I think I have what you are looking for” he said with a smile. Lucas came over and gave the big man a hug “So, how was your first day as a super spy, heard you almost wasted Howie” he said conspiratorially. Lucas shook his head still smiling “I don’t know which to be more disturbed by, the fact that you used the term wasted or that the guy who followed me was named Howie” he said and laughed. Sally lightly slapped him on the shoulder “Oh stop, Howie is a sweety” he said and Rollie piped up from across the room “You mean your sweet on Howie” Sally rolled his eyes “Sweep you and shush” with feined irritation but the smile retuned quickly. “Follow me and we will find you something to hit repeatedly” and Lucas did as they descended further into the bowels of the club.

Sally unlocked the door to a room at the very back of the club, once opened Lucas entered to find a concrete cavern the size of a small warehouse. Looking around the junk filled room he whisted at the sheer size of the place. “How am I suppoed to find anything in here Aunt Sally?” he asked . Sally found the lightswitch and tenty old halogen bulbs came to life barely lighting the big space.

“I know where everything is, follow me dear” he said and walked him around the large shelves and covered items that were strewn about the room. Finally he came to an area in the middle of the room and Sally threw off a dust cover “viola” he said and there in the middle of the pile was an archery target, old and worn but still usable and a martial arts Wing Chun self-standing dummy, along with a full body dummy he could use for knife training. “Don’t tell me this just happen to be here, all three the exact items I needed” Lucas asked amazed. Sally laughed “No, I had Chow grab them before you got here and bring them in but had you there for a minute didn’t I” he asked pointing a finger playfully. “If you want a few Rollie can help you carry them back to the store.

An hour later a winded Rollie and Lucas put all three items in the middle of the floor of his room. “Damn, I didn’t think it would be that heavy” Rollie said collapsing on Lucas’s bed. He looked at the young man and laughed. “You need to start lifting buddy” and then slid down the wall blowing out a puff of air. They both rested for a good fifteen minutes before Rollie begged off stating he had more work that needed done before he quit for the day but promising to come by if Lucas showed him how to use the dummy. He agreed, liking the young man already and if he was honest, in need of a friend his own age. Once he had them setup, he was also surprised to find a pair of MMA gloves and two sets of practice fighting knives, Sally must of stuck them in there that old sly dog he thought shaking his head.



Four hours later Job opened the door and leaned in to find his young friend drenched in sweat and going through various katas on the wing chun dummy. Job could see his hair matted to his head and the perspiration running down his back. “How long have you been at this” surprised at the kid’s stamina. Lucas shrugged “for a while”. Job just shook his head “We leave for dinner in an hour” he said seriously “Wear the knives” and then he shut the door.

An hour later Lucas was showered and dressed and ready to go. They walked down to the checkpoint, the sun now setting over the poverty bloc as a light snow began to fall once again this cold November night. Approaching the check point Job turned to his young companion “I have us going to a meeting downtown, just nod your head” he whispered as they approached. It took a few moments, but the guards waved them through and the two began to walk towards the DC mall. “Unless we are in a hurry, no cabs, we don’t want records of our travel’s” he stated, and Lucas felt guilty about earlier and consoled himself before he had been on “Xanadu Imports” business. “The contact we are going to meet works in Justice, so if someone has an active investigation or working on a deal with someone, she would know my guess is someone folded and might be selling out the part of the network they know, if this is true we need to know who so we can scatter that part of the network before they move in” Job said talking to fill the time as they walked. “What would happen if they get the people in the network?” Lucas asked and got a severe look from Job. “Its treason to do what we do, they would shoot them, on the spot” he said Lucas hanging his head, he knew but there was a marked difference from theory and having it actually happen he thought. They crossed the street at the intersection and approached a black awning with a bull on it as they drew closer Job stopped and turned to Lucas “Okay, ground rules, let me do the talking okay” he said and got a nod from his young friend.

He turned and spied a woman in a heavy coat waiting out front of the restaurant, as he watched she walked in the front door. “She is in, we wait five minutes and then join her” he said.

They stood there for a few minutes and with a nod from Job they approached the restaurant and as they reached the edge of the building, the whole world exploded in brick and fire.

Job threw himself back taking Lucas down with him as fire reighed all around them, a piece of molten brick touched Lucas’s arm and he screamed as it seared the flesh, his good eye tearing up from pain.

Job stood and pulled Lucas up with him “Get up, we have to move” he said deadpan and pulled the dazed younger man along and after a moment Lucas shrugged his grip off now moving on his own momentum. Once they were a block away from the devastation he whirled on Job “What the fuck was that?” he hissed looking over Job’s shoulder and spied a torso still smoldering in the middle of the pedestrian way. That image seared into his mind and it would be months before he would be able to forget that one scene. Job spoke with anger and sorrow infused in his choked-up tone “Someone found out Angela was talking to us, that bomb was meant to kill all of us” he said and continued to walk. “Who would do that? Who could do that? I mean if it was the government, they would just arrest her right?” he asked hopefully.

Job whirled on his friend “Oh wake up kid, that was the government, they don’t care about people, this is the Vipers this is just their fucking style” he said shaking his head Lucas could see the irrational anger as he tried to maintain control of himself. “What the hell is a Viper?” he asked, hoping not to get the brunt of the old man’s temper.

“Department of Security Special Security Force of SSF, we just call them Vipers” they are the governments shock troops, they kill, made disappear and frame anyone who gets in the way of the CEO’s agenda.” he started “They killed everyone in that Restaurant just in the hopes they would kill Angela and her contact, but even shutting up Angela would be a win, they will spin it as a gas explosion or maybe they will blame us again” he said. “They do that?” he asked and then distantly remembering a story about a suicide bomber walking into a coffee shop supposedly a member of the resistance. Job looked at him disgustedly “No we don’t bomb anyone, we are an intelligence gathering network, we make payoffs and occasionally we assassinate when it suits us, but never without a reason and we never use bombs or kill innocents, it’s not our way” Lucas finished. The two walked back to the store in silence both brooding at the possibilities of what this meant. Once the door closed Lucas checked to ensure the box was closed on the phones and watches and then turned to his friend. “Whatever Angela knew, it was big, I mean big enough to nuke a restaurant” he stated remembering the exact message she had sent to them.

“Traitor, danger close” he repeated and then looked at Job “What did she mean?” he asked. Job looked at him and his face fell “That means we have someone among the inner circle who has turned on us” he whispered.

An hour later the two of them Sat in Sally’s club each with a stiff drink in front of them. Sally, Victoria and Rollie sat with them all nursing drinks and staring off into space “What do we do?” Victoria asked shaking her head, she had known Angie, they had gone to school together ten years prior and the tear tracks were still fresh on her face. She gulped down the light brown liquid and grabbed the bottle for another. Sally looked like he was about to protest and then rescinded opting instead to pouring another as well.

“We can’t do anything, we can warn the safehouses and the cells, but until something happens, we don’t know which part of the network is in danger” Job whispered feeling powerless at the moment. Sally turned to Victoria her Blonde hair hanging over her face to hide her crying, but Lucas could see her shoulders hitching as she sat there, gripping the glass way too hard. “V, I need you to send the code alert sweetie” Sally said gently prodding her. With her Blonde hair still in her face she nodded, her hair bobbing. She got up and stumbled to the back room, keeping her face hidden from the group.

Lucas looked around curiously. “What code?” he asked “I thought we don’t use computers” his voice alarmed. Job turned to him “in an emergency we post a single word on a forum, that alerts everyone to be on guard.” He said and then went back to staring at his drink. Sally sighed “Now all we can do is wait and see”. They stayed there sitting silent and drinking for the next two hours, the club remaining closed.

With nothing more to do and the entire group already well on their way to getting drunk, they called it a night agreeing to regroup the next day.

Lucas awoke early the next morning to a commotion in the living room and came out to find Sally and Rollie already there, both their faces looked grim as Job sat their head in his hands. “What’s happened” Lucas asked walking into the living area. Rollie turned towards the TV and pointed. Lucas looked as the state news network reported on an explosion at an abandoned distillery in Baltimore early this morning. “What is this?” Lucas asked not connecting the dots. Job looked up, he looked practically sick “That’s our Baltimore safehouse, and our Richmond safehouse was blown up as well, both within twenty minutes of each other. They are making a statement, they are two separate networks so whoever they have that turned, is high up in our network” he finished. “The attacks narrow it to about a hundred people” Job finished.

“Whats the plan?” Lucas asked Sally slumped on the couch, he was wearing a black tracksuit, in fact this was the first time he had seen the man out of his kimono. “I knew both Brad and David who ran those houses personally, there were three families we were moving to Canada in the Baltimore safehouse, a mother and father and four children” he said rubbing his bloodshot eyes. It was obvious he had been crying. “Okay, so whats the plan” Lucas asked again. “We have put out queries to find out who isn’t around and if anyone of the one hundred has gone missing” Job said “other then that there is nothing we can do yet, but if there are more attacks then we are going to have enact our safety protocol, but we are not there yet, we just need to hope that this is the end of it” he said. “We have never had a breach like this, not in the history of the organization, we have managed to keep any reprisals isolated to a single cell or safehouse, never have two separate networks come under attack”. But with messages past via paper it is going to be a few days until we get any more information.

They spent the day walking around aimlessly, not much getting done as the group digested the ramifications of this attack. Rollie went each morning to check the dead drops , and each day came back empty, until the third day.

He rushed into the apartment with a small stack of paper and without a word went to work decoding the messages, as he finished, he handed each to Job who would read it and pass it along.

An hour later they all sat there staring at the stack of notes. “That’s everyone, no one is missing and so far as wel can tell no one has been turned, two more houses one in North Carolina and the entire cell in West Virginia have gone dark” Job said relaying everything they had learned.

Rollie decoded the last message “Guys did you say West Virginia is dark?” he asked holding the piece of paper. Job nodded and looked at him. “yes, why” Rollie walked over and slowly handed the last page at Job “We have the orphanage in West Virginia don’t we, they checked in and said strange cars have been seen for the past few days” he whispered.

Job sat up “If they know about the orphanage, oh Jesus” he said his face going white. Lucas looked around the room “Someone want to tell me what the hell the orphanage is”. Sally looked at him his face fallen “We have a complex where we take care of orphans of people killed or jailed by the government until they are old enough to move across the border or get new Identities, its full of young children Lucas” he whispered and then the note’s significance hit him like a meteor. “We have to help them” he said, and Job nodded “It might be too late already” he said but Lucas waved a dismissal “We have to try dammit” he said. Sally nodded to Rollie. “Go with him, take my car and get down there, see if we can move the children, I will work out where while you are on the way there” he said standing. A plan forming and giving some small hope to the group. Rollie nodded and then tapped Lucas on the shoulder “Let’s go, now” he said moving towards the door with a purpose.

They walked out of the checkpoint and two blocks to a parking garage as fast as they could without drawing attention. Rollie walked to the covered mound and threw off the cover to the Black luxury sedan. Getting in he started the car, Lucas piling into the passenger seat as it lifted off, joining traffic in the skyway heading as fast as they could to get to West Virginia before it was too late.



They arrived in the small town of Falling Waters West Virginia as dusk settled over the small town. “There is an old mill on the outskirts that we run, I will land the car a mile from it and we will finish the trip on foot” Rollie said and Lucas nodding “Good, we can recon before we move in.” he said, checking the knives. Once they landed Rollie popped the trunk. “Sally has some special items in case of emergency, and this is definitely an emergency” he said pulling out a small metal case and hefting it onto the ground. Rollie pulled out two items that Lucas could only describe as full body Black wetsuits and he picked one up and looked at it curiously. “It makes you invisible to ocular sensors, like the kind the military use, if they try to see us in Infrared or most other filters, they use to track enemies, you won’t show up, it’s like being invisible in the dark” he said. Lucas nodded with approval and began to change. Rollie also handed him a mask and a pair of boots. “The mask will also allow you to see in low light and the boots are sound dampening, the entire suite is still in R and D for the military, but its suppose to allow you to get close to the enemy before they know your there” Lucas approved, if the Vipers were there, then they would have guns and the two of them needed every advantage they could get.

Rollie reached over hitting a button on the underside of the helmet. It looked like a slim version of a motor cross helmet, kind of like he had seen on TV when he watched the old documentaries on extreme sports, the helmet had a mouthguard with vertical slits as well as a built in Visor , of course half of it was useless to him having only one good eye but the part he could see out of gave the landscape a greyed out look, but it enhanced the light almost like he was walking around at dusk instead of the dead of night. “How is it they don’t have these suits, they seem pretty useful” Lucas asked Rollie just shrugged “Something about the suits being too expensive per soldier or something, we got them from one of our contacts within the Department of Security” he simply said. Lucas hoped he was right; it would be odd to walk around not seeing anyone and having them not see them as well. He had a mental image of two groups of people running into each other and wondering what the hell they hit and smiled to himself.

Twenty minutes later the two of them, fully suited took off at a trot towards the mill. “Let’s hope we just end up scaring some little kids in these stupid suits” Rollie whispered just now showing wear from the run. Lucas could hear his labored breathing. “Slow down Rollie, we need to be fresh if there is trouble” he said, controlling his own breathing.  Rollie paused for a moment, putting his hands on his knees he fought to gain control of his own breathing. Lucas began pacing, looking off in the distance he could see the silhouette of the old factory standing just the other side of the hill they were on.

After a moment the two began moving forward, working through the underbrush as fast as they could without making too much noise. As they approached the outer wall of the large worn brick structure Lucas snapped his fist up, giving the military hold signal. Rollie moved a little further until Lucas turned around and mouthed the word “hold”. He took for granted that Dyson had taught him so much and so well he thought. Holding his breath, he listened for what had caught his attention. He waited for a good two minutes and just as he was about to move forward, thinking it was a trick of his imagination, he heard it again. A radio squawk from somewhere in front of them. Lucas lowered himself into a squat and Rollie did the same after a moment.

If Lucas listened carefully, he could hear the sound of light footsteps both in the general direction of the radio noise and then shifting his head a little to try and pick up as much ambient noise as possible, he heard another set of soft shuffling step to his right. Shit he thought, they were hear. The Vipers that Job had talked about must be onsite, that means they were here to destroy the orphanage, from the stories he had heard Lucas didn’t think they would spare the kids. Lucas moved his helmet through the area of underbrush in front of him and stopped dead, he was squatting at waist height to a solder in full combat gear not two feet from him and facing in his direction. He did his best to keep calm as he stared up at the face of a soldier wearing some type of Visor, it was more like a full face shield but it was smoky colored. The soldier appeared to be looking directly at him, however he didn’t react at all. Rollie began to move forward to see why Lucas had stopped but he shot his hand out against his friends chest stopping him, he felt his way up his friends front to what he hoped was his shoulder, but there was no way he would be taking his eyes of this guy and gripped his shoulder, hoping he would get the message.

But the shuffling in the brush had elicited a reaction from the guard, who began to look out over the woods , he poked the rifle he carried at the underbrush not two inched from Lucas and then shrugged, turning to face the old warehouse.

He looked to his left and right and could make out six soldiers two were on either side, probably as guards to ensure no one left the building and four were gathered around a case, they looked to be preparing for entry. He didn’t have a lot of time.

As quietly as he could Lucas removed one of the obsidian blades from the small of his back. Recalling the knife training he had spent years perfecting while under the tutelage of Dyson. With lightning speed, he stood up and stepped forward bringing him to stand directly at the back of this guard. He put a hand on the front of the helmet and at the same time slid the knife into the base of the soldier’s neck, twisting the blade once it had entered. Lucas could hear the synthetic stone scrap along the Vertebrae until he couldn’t push forward anymore.

The soldier, without making a sound simply dropped. Letting go of the knife he grabbed the dead soldier by the back of his harness and dragged him into the underbrush. Looking back, it seemed none of the guards noticed him missing, yet. But it wouldn’t take long before they would be ready to go and notice one of their own was no longer there. He gently laid the dead body into the underbrush, doing his best not to make a sound. Turning to Rollie he told him what he had seen. “Can you deal with the other guard and I will grab the guys at the crate” He asked. Hoping Rollie had some training, the young ebony man simply nodded. The helmet and visor making him look more like a gothic version of a motocross rider then a soldier and he began to make his way along the Woodline, deep enough so that any noise wouldn’t attract any unwanted attention.

Lucas moved down behind his friend until he was parallel with the group at the crate. He could hear there whispers and laughter. Anger rose in his chest as he thought about these sick bastards joking before going in to kill defenseless children. Up until now he had feared the government, been annoyed with the government but not until this moment had he really loathed his government. He would not mourn these men; they would not weigh on his conscience for the death he was about to deliver upon them. They deserved to die and so much worse he thought. His fists clenching around the hilt of the knife that still dripped blood from his first victim of the night. Lucas quietly withdrew a second blade, never taking his eyes off the other guard as he stood there facing the building not knowing this would be the last thing he would see.

A moment later Lucas watched impressed as Rollie executed the same move he himself had just done. Once he had begun to drag the soldier into the underbrush Lucas was moving, Not caring about sound as he burst from the tree line, all four of the soldiers turning towards the trees as his footfalls reached them.

As if confused they stood there cocking there heads and trying to see into the underbrush, as if confused at the noise. But Lucas pushed that out of his mind. He quickly made up the ground between himself and his victims. Lashing out he severed the tendons on the inside of the elbow of the first soldier. As he did that his other hand drove the knife up into the soft throat and palate of the same guard. He quickly withdrew both blades the blood that sprayed from the guards throat looked more like oil in the greyed out viewer of the helmet then actual blood. As the first guard fell, the other three snapped their attention to him, bringing up their guns as the guard fell for seemingly no reason. For the moment he had moving between one guard to the next. Lucas thought it odd that all they would have to do is remove their helmet and they would see him but he remembered Job and Dyson’s words “Technology has made them lazy, they rely on it too much” and now he finally understood what they meant. Lucas took one more step, putting himself to the guards left. With a quick downward slash along the ceratoid artery he stepped behind him. The guards hand shooting up to his neck as he unleashed a gurgling scream. As he took another step he pivoted and with the same Blade drove it into the third guards throat, feeling it scrape the man’s Adam’s apple as it sliced through his windpipe like butter.

Before Lucas had reached the third guard Rollie was there, coming up behind him and inserting his blade under the right arm in the soft area of the suit he wore. From the look his friend drove it up and into the guard’s lung and then sliced downward. The gurgling and labored breath the guard took confirmed Lucas’s conclusion.

It had only taken all of twenty seconds, but the entire hit team lie dead at their feet.

Rollie knelt down rummaging through the crate of gear. Most he left but there were a few things he grabbed and producing a folded empty black satchel out of a cargo pocket on the suit he filled it, and then tied it to his waist. Once he was done, he motioned for them to enter the factory. Their heads on a swivel the two approached the large wooden doors that was the entrance to the old cotton mill. Once they had reached the door Lucas raised an arm to knock but Rollie grabbed it, shaking his head. Motioning to his friend he stepped back and let Rollie take the lead.

He slammed his fist four times, paused and then three more times against the door. Rollie had hit the thick wood so hard, Lucas could hear it reverberating through the large building. They heard muted footsteps which seemed to grow a little louder as someone approached the entrance. They stopped and there was silence for a moment. Finally, a female voice with a deep southern accent asked, “What is the meaning of life?” Rollie leaned in to ensure that his voice would be heard through the door and answered, “forty seven”. Lucas wasn’t sure what the hell that meant, but it seemed to be the right answer. The large door opened quietly and easily on well-oiled hinges and as it passed him, he could easily see why they would need to keep the hinges maintained. The door was a good six inches thick.

The petite Hispanic woman stood there in a thick nightgown, her black hair pulled back in a tight pony tail holding a large frying pan, as if she was going to hit the two. Rollie put his hands up “Marta, its Rollie, it’s me” he said removing his helmet and smiling at the woman. She visible relaxed and lowered the frying pan. “What the hell are you doing here Cabrone” she asked shocked to see him all the way out here in West Virginia. Lucas couldn’t help but notice the use of the Hispanic slang and smiled at the sound of hit coming from someone who sounded like she had grown up somewhere deep in Georgia instead of Tiahuanaco. Rollie pointed over his shoulder and the short woman produced a flashlight, as soon as she clicked it on. Lucas’s visor darkened a little allowing him to maintain his night vision. She played it around the crate and over the bodies of the assault troops sent to kill them and gasped.

She ushered the two in the factory and closed and bolted the door. “What’s going on, we reported seeing strange people, but I thought we were just under surveillance, not marked for death” she asked all humor gone from her voice. Rollie shook his head “They sent a damn Viper squad to blow this place up Marta” he said reaching into his satchel and producing something that looked like modeling clay and then putting it back in. “We need to get everyone dressed and ready to go, Sally is sending transport now, we don’t have a lot of time , these guys are not going to check in and this area will be lousy with drones come morning” he finished.
